headline_findings.finding: SINGLE_SOURCE_VALIDATION requires requested_source_universe_ref and records it in the material and replay identity, but evaluate_bound_positioned_subject_possibility validates the QUERY's source against the whole admitted set. A single-source binding made for A evaluates B and returns EXACT_SUPPORTED with the same result hash as the exhaustive binding.

'positive_powers_exactly_two' / 'The two positive powers, exactly' is false of the declared public surface, which has five returning callables including evaluate_bound_positioned_subject_possibility (a full F8 evaluation through the binding) and verify_service_f8_scope_binding_replay. The court itself classifies the evaluator as a power.

The bound_to_requested_release: False provenance branch is dead code: the adopted owner stamps every decision with the request's release, so a receipt always presents exactly one release. The binder's release safety therefore rests on the owner invariant, and the branch would fail OPEN rather than closed if the owner ever became per-decision-release.

Four claim/evidence mismatches: docstring says 'the three that are attempted-against refuse' (seven exist); docstring says 'There is no third' (a third returning function exists); the conditioner AST scan omits six F8 attributes the binder does read while claiming to prove a general property; and requested_currentness_claim accepts an unpinned caller vocabulary.

The environment freeze-identity claim is honestly disclosed as reconstructed-equivalent but is not independently checkable in this checkout: the governed venv, the DARWIN_ANCHOR_RUNTIME lock path and the referenced interpreter are all absent.

The write-terrain guards silently pytest.skip when an owner file is absent or git/hash-object is unavailable, so an all-green run can hide a guard that never ran. In this environment they ran and passed.
